senses.gloss: A unit of scoring in a game, contest, or grading system.
examples: The Lakers won by three *points*.
She lost a *point* for turning the paper in late.
Each correct answer is worth two *points*.

senses.gloss: The main idea or purpose of what someone says or does.
examples: I don't see the *point* of arguing about it.
Get to the *point* — we only have ten minutes.
That's a fair *point*, but the numbers say otherwise.

senses.gloss: A particular moment or stage in a process.
examples: At that *point* I decided to quit.
We reached a *point* where nobody trusted anyone.
There's no turning back at this *point*.

senses.gloss: A short piece of practical advice.
examples: Can you give me a few *pointers* on my resume?
The coach offered one *pointer* that fixed my swing.
Her *pointers* about interviewing turned out to be useful.

senses.gloss: A stick, needle, or arrow used to show where something is.
examples: He tapped the map with a wooden *pointer*.
Move the *pointer* over the icon and click.
The dial's *pointer* stopped just below the red zone.

senses.gloss: A metal rod used to stir a fire.
examples: He pushed the log back with a *poker*.
A brass *poker* hung beside the fireplace.
She stirred the coals with the *poker* until they glowed.

senses.gloss: A long slender rod of wood or metal, usually standing upright.
examples: A crew was replacing a rotten telephone *pole*.
He hung the flag from a *pole* on the porch.
Two tent *poles* snapped in the wind.

senses.gloss: Either end of a magnet or battery, where the force is concentrated.
examples: Two magnets snap together unless you turn one *pole* around.
Attach the red clamp to the positive *pole* of the battery.
Opposite *poles* attract each other.

senses.gloss: A game played on a cloth-covered table in which balls are hit into pockets with a long stick.
examples: We shot *pool* in the basement all afternoon.
There's a *pool* table in the back of the bar.
He hustled tourists at *pool* for spending money.

senses.gloss: A shared supply of money, people, or things that others can draw on.
examples: The company draws from a small *pool* of translators.
Everyone chipped in for the office betting *pool*.
A shrinking *pool* of applicants worries the school district.

senses.gloss: A small amount of liquid lying on a surface.
examples: A *pool* of oil spread under the truck.
Blood had collected in a *pool* by the door.
Candle wax dried in *pools* on the table.

senses.gloss: A style of popular music with catchy tunes, aimed at a wide audience.
examples: She grew up listening to eighties *pop*.
The station plays nothing but *pop*.
His new album leans more toward *pop* than country.

senses.gloss: A short sharp sound like a cork coming out of a bottle.
examples: The cork came out with a loud *pop*.
We heard three *pops* and then silence.
The balloon burst with a *pop*.

senses.gloss: Government money spent on local projects mainly to please voters.
examples: Critics called the highway money pure *pork*.
The bill was loaded with *pork* for a dozen districts.
Every senator claims to hate *pork* until it comes home.

senses.gloss: A dark heavy beer made with roasted malt.
examples: He ordered a *porter* and a plate of fries.
This brewery's *porter* tastes like coffee.
They have three *porters* on tap tonight.

senses.gloss: A part of something larger.
examples: A large *portion* of the budget goes to salaries.
Only a small *portion* of the land is farmed.
She donates a *portion* of every paycheck.

senses.gloss: A way of behaving that is not sincere, put on to impress people.
examples: His modesty is just a *pose*.
The tough-guy act is a *pose* he learned from movies.
Behind the *pose* of indifference, he was terrified.

senses.gloss: A strong upright piece of wood or metal fixed in the ground.
examples: The gate hangs on a rotting *post*.
He tied the horse to a *post* by the barn.
The ball bounced off the goal *post*.

senses.gloss: A job or official position.
examples: She left her *post* at the embassy last spring.
He held the *post* of treasurer for nine years.
Three teaching *posts* went unfilled.

senses.gloss: The place where a soldier or guard is stationed, or an army base.
examples: The guard never left his *post*.
Families live on the *post* in base housing.
He was transferred to a *post* in Texas.

senses.gloss: An official position or attitude taken toward something.
examples: The company's legal *posture* softened after the ruling.
Both countries adopted a defensive *posture*.
It was a bargaining *posture*, not a real offer.

senses.gloss: Marijuana.
examples: The whole car smelled like *pot*.
*Pot* is legal in this state now.
He got caught with a little *pot* in high school.

senses.gloss: All the money bet in a single hand of cards, or a shared fund collected from a group.
examples: She pushed all her chips into the *pot*.
The *pot* was over two hundred dollars by the last round.
Everyone put five bucks in the *pot* for pizza.

senses.gloss: A clay or plastic container that a plant grows in.
examples: The basil needs a bigger *pot*.
Clay *pots* dry out faster than plastic ones.
She carried the *pots* inside before the frost.

senses.gloss: The unit of money used in Britain.
examples: The room cost ninety *pounds* a night.
The *pound* fell against the dollar again.
I still have a few *pounds* left from the trip.

senses.gloss: A place where stray animals or towed cars are held.
examples: We adopted her from the city *pound*.
His car spent two days at the *pound*.
Someone found the dog and took it to the *pound*.

senses.gloss: The # key on a telephone.
examples: Enter your account number, then press *pound*.
Dial the extension followed by the *pound* sign.
Leave a message and hit *pound* when you're done.

senses.gloss: The building and grounds occupied by a business or organization, used in the plural.
examples: No food or drink is allowed on the *premises*.
Security escorted him off the *premises*.
The firm moved to larger *premises* downtown.

senses.gloss: An extra amount added to the usual price or value of something.
examples: Buyers pay a *premium* for a corner unit.
The stock is trading at a *premium* to its book value.
Fresh fish commands a *premium* this far inland.

senses.gloss: A thing given to someone as a gift.
examples: She opened her birthday *presents* after dinner.
I still need to buy a *present* for my nephew.
The *present* came wrapped in plain brown paper.

senses.gloss: A short clip shown before a movie to advertise another one.
examples: We got there early to catch the *previews*.
The *preview* gave away the whole ending.
There were twenty minutes of *previews* before the film started.

senses.gloss: An early look at something before it is generally available.
examples: Reporters got a *preview* of the report on Monday.
The app shows a *preview* of the message.
Here's a quick *preview* of what we'll cover tomorrow.

senses.gloss: A person who is easily cheated or harmed by someone else.
examples: Lonely widows are easy *prey* for these scammers.
New arrivals became *prey* for anyone selling fake papers.
He saw the tourists as *prey*.

senses.gloss: Something unpleasant that has to be accepted in order to get something else.
examples: Losing his privacy was the *price* of fame.
Long hours are the *price* you pay for this job.
Freedom came at a terrible *price*.

senses.gloss: A whole number that can be divided evenly only by itself and one.
examples: Seventeen is a *prime*.
The list of *primes* starts 2, 3, 5, 7.
She wrote a program that hunts for very large *primes*.

senses.gloss: A person or company whose business is printing books, posters, and other material.
examples: The manuscript is at the *printer* now.
A local *printer* made the wedding invitations.
The *printer* wants the final files by Friday.

senses.gloss: A solid figure whose two ends are identical parallel shapes joined by flat sides.
examples: A cereal box is a rectangular *prism*.
Find the volume of the *prism*.
The kids built *prisms* out of cardboard.

senses.gloss: A thorough official investigation.
examples: A federal *probe* into the contracts is under way.
The *probe* found no evidence of fraud.
Two *probes* were opened after the crash.

senses.gloss: An unmanned spacecraft sent to study a planet or other object in space.
examples: The *probe* sent back the first close-up of the surface.
Ground control lost contact with the *probe* in March.
Two *probes* are still transmitting after forty years.

senses.gloss: Something that has come about as the result of a particular cause or set of conditions.
examples: His caution is a *product* of a rough childhood.
The law was the *product* of years of argument.
That attitude is a *product* of the time she grew up in.

senses.gloss: The number you get by multiplying numbers together.
examples: The *product* of six and seven is forty-two.
Write the *product* in the last column.
Both *products* came out the same.

senses.gloss: A group of government-owned apartment buildings for low-income families, usually in the plural.
examples: He grew up in the *projects* on the South Side.
The city is tearing down two *projects* next year.
Kids from the *project* walked to school together.

senses.gloss: Signs that someone or something will be successful later on.
examples: The young pitcher shows real *promise*.
Her first novel was full of *promise*.
The project began with great *promise* and ended badly.

senses.gloss: A word, question, or picture given to start a piece of writing or a discussion.
examples: The teacher put a new writing *prompt* on the board.
Each essay *prompt* is worth twenty minutes.
We pulled *prompts* out of a jar.

senses.gloss: A reminder of the next words, given to an actor who has forgotten a line.
examples: He froze on stage and waited for a *prompt*.
She needed a *prompt* in the second act.
A whispered *prompt* saved the scene.

senses.gloss: A pole or beam used to hold something up.
examples: Wooden *props* held up the sagging ceiling.
He wedged a *prop* under the loaded branch.
The miners set new *props* along the tunnel.

senses.gloss: Credit or respect given to someone, used in the plural.
examples: Give the guy *props* for showing up at all.
She deserves *props* for finishing the race.
He got *props* from everyone in the room.

senses.gloss: A statement or action showing that you object to something.
examples: He signed the contract under *protest*.
Her *protests* were ignored by the committee.
The lawyer entered a formal *protest*.

senses.gloss: The soft juicy part of a fruit or vegetable.
examples: I like orange juice with plenty of *pulp*.
Scoop the *pulp* out of the melon.
Strain the juice to get rid of the *pulp*.

senses.gloss: Cheap sensational fiction, originally printed on rough paper.
examples: He wrote detective *pulp* for a penny a word.
The store keeps a shelf of old *pulp* by the window.
Critics dismissed the novel as *pulp*.

senses.gloss: A single short burst of sound, light, or electricity.
examples: The machine sends a *pulse* down the wire.
The laser fires in very short *pulses*.
A *pulse* of radio noise wiped out the signal.

senses.gloss: A woman's plain shoe with a raised heel and no strap or laces.
examples: She wore black *pumps* with the suit.
These *pumps* kill my feet by noon.
A pair of low *pumps* sat by the door.

senses.gloss: A hard blow with the fist.
examples: He took a *punch* to the jaw.
One *punch* ended the fight.
She threw two quick *punches* at the bag.

senses.gloss: A tool or machine for making holes.
examples: Use the three-hole *punch* on those handouts.
The *punch* left a clean round hole in the leather.
He kept a set of *punches* in the bottom drawer.

senses.gloss: Forceful quality that makes something get attention.
examples: The ending lacks *punch*.
A few short sentences give the paragraph more *punch*.
The commercial has real *punch*.

senses.gloss: A rude, worthless young man.
examples: Some *punk* keyed my car.
He was a scared little *punk* back then.
The *punks* on the corner scattered when the cruiser pulled in.

senses.gloss: A person or government secretly controlled by someone else.
examples: The general installed a *puppet* in the capital.
Voters saw him as a *puppet* of the oil companies.
The council became a *puppet* of the mayor's office.

senses.gloss: A child being taught in a school.
examples: Each teacher has about twenty-five *pupils*.
She was the best *pupil* in her class.
The *pupils* line up in the hallway after lunch.

senses.gloss: Freedom from moral wrongdoing.
examples: The sect preached *purity* and hard work.
He questioned the *purity* of their motives.
White is worn there as a sign of *purity*.

senses.gloss: The prize money offered in a boxing match, race, or tournament.
examples: The winner takes a *purse* of two million.
The *purse* for the derby went up again this year.
The two fighters split the *purse* evenly.

senses.gloss: An activity that someone spends time on, used mostly in the plural.
examples: He went back to his scientific *pursuits*.
Weekends are for outdoor *pursuits*.
Reading was her main *pursuit* that winter.

senses.gloss: Someone who pretends to have medical skill.
examples: The clinic turned out to be run by a *quack*.
Don't waste money on some *quack* selling cures online.
Nineteenth-century *quacks* sold colored water as medicine.

senses.gloss: The large muscle at the front of the thigh, usually in the plural.
examples: My *quads* are sore from squats.
He tore a *quad* during the game.
Stretch your *quads* before you run.

senses.gloss: An animal or person that is being hunted or chased.
examples: The hawk circled above its *quarry*.
The detectives lost their *quarry* in the crowd.
The hounds tracked the *quarry* for two miles.
